content:
I just finished a little project I've been working on for a while: I've proven there are 43,252,003,274,489,856,000 solvable 3 x 3 Rubik's cubes!

This would be a relatively simple combinatorial problem, if not for the solvability condition. If you break apart a Rubik's cube and put it back together, you're not guaranteed to get something that can be solved! In fact, the solvable Rubik's cubes are precisely those in the kernel of a certain group homomorphism into ℤ₂ × ℤ₂ × ℤ₃. One direction is simple - we can show via direct computation that any valid move preserves this value. But proving the converse requires building an algorithm to solve any Rubik's cube.

My proof is entirely constructive, not in the strict sense of not employing choice, but in the sense that all the functions can be evaluated. This means that you can input a Rubik's cube sticker by sticker using the auxiliary Sticker.toRubik, and use #eval to have Lean print out a solution for it.

Repository: https://github.com/vihdzp/rubik-lean4
